rationale.subject: Profile 'campus_lan'
rationale.justification: 3 buildings and 1600 endpoints on one campus: a separate distribution layer would add a switch pair per building without improving fault isolation. The L3 core switch acts as distribution, terminating every VLAN's SVI, while access switches stay pure L2 with RSTP.

rationale.subject: BLDG-A horizontal drop
rationale.justification: Run of 90 m is within the 100 m 10GBASE-T channel limit (90 m permanent link + 10 m cords). Cat6a's 500 MHz rating supports 10 Gb/s over the full length and carries IEEE 802.3bt PoE (up to 90 W) for APs, phones and cameras; fiber would add transceiver cost with no reach benefit.

rationale.subject: CORE-SW1 <-> BLDG-A uplink
rationale.justification: Run of 45 m is within the 100 m 10GBASE-T channel limit (90 m permanent link + 10 m cords). rationale.subject: BLDG-A
rationale.justification: 650 endpoints / 48 ports = 14 switches (2 stack(s); StackWise max 9 members). 30 PoE APs x 30 W (IEEE 802.3at Class 4) = 900 W PoE budget, so PoE+ capable access switches are required; IP phones share the PC port via the voice VLAN.

rationale.subject: CORE-SW1 <-> BLDG-B uplink
rationale.justification: Run of 180 m exceeds the 100 m copper limit (IEEE 802.3an) but is within the 400 m reach of 10GBASE-SR on OM4. At 850 nm the low-cost VCSEL source is limited by modal dispersion, not loss; OM4's 4700 MHz*km effective modal bandwidth sustains 10 Gb/s to 400 m. Channel loss 1.54 dB (0.180 km x 3.0 dB/km + 2 x 0.5 dB connectors) <= 2.9 dB SR budget.

rationale.subject: CORE-SW1 <-> BLDG-B uplink
rationale.justification: Required bandwidth 20 Gb/s exceeds a single 10G lane; ceil(20/10) = 2 member links are bundled with LACP so traffic is hashed across them and a member failure only reduces capacity.

rationale.subject: STAFF-A
rationale.justification: 480 hosts + 2 (network, broadcast) = 482 addresses; smallest power of two >= that is 2^9 = 512 -> /23 (mask 255.255.254.0, wildcard 0.0.1.255). Gateway 10.10.0.1 (first usable), broadcast 10.10.1.255. Utilization 480/510 = 94.1%.

rationale.subject: CORE-EDGE-P2P
rationale.justification: Point-to-point link: RFC 3021 /31 uses both addresses as hosts (no network/broadcast needed on a 2-node link), saving 50% vs a /30.

rationale.subject: LO-CORE-SW1
rationale.justification: Router loopback / router-ID: a /32 host route is stable and always up.

rationale.subject: LO-EDGE-RTR1
rationale.justification: Router loopback / router-ID: a /32 host route is stable and always up.

rationale.subject: campus root 10.10.0.0/16
rationale.justification: Requests were sorted by required block size (largest first) and placed sequentially on their natural bit boundaries, which guarantees zero overlap and no fragmentation. 3044 of 65536 addresses consumed (4.6% of the block); host efficiency 2268/3026 usable = 75.0%. Remaining 62492 addresses are contiguous at the top of the block for growth.

rationale.subject: Interior gateway protocol
rationale.justification: One site / one autonomous system with 12 subnets (< 50). A single backbone area keeps every router's LSDB identical and small, so SPF (Dijkstra) runs in milliseconds and link-state flooding gives sub-second convergence after a failure. Multi-area design would add ABR complexity with no scaling benefit at this size; distance-vector protocols (RIP) were rejected for slow, hop-count-limited convergence.

rationale.subject: VLAN segmentation
rationale.justification: Each traffic class (per-building staff data, voice, corporate Wi-Fi, guest, AP management, servers, network management) gets its own VLAN/broadcast domain so broadcast load is contained and inter-VLAN traffic is forced through the L3 core where ACLs apply. Per-building data VLANs keep broadcast domains under ~500 hosts.

rationale.subject: Trunk hardening
rationale.decision: Pruned trunks, native VLAN 999, DTP off
rationale.justification: Every trunk carries only the VLANs that exist in that building ('switchport trunk allowed vlan <list>', never 'all'), uses unused native VLAN 999 so untagged frames land nowhere (defeats double-tag VLAN hopping), and disables DTP with 'switchport nonegotiate' so a host cannot negotiate a trunk.

rationale.subject: Spanning tree
rationale.justification: Redundant uplinks create L2 loops; RSTP's proposal/agreement handshake converges in < 1 s versus 30-50 s for legacy 802.1D. The core is pinned as root (priority 4096) for every VLAN so traffic follows the designed path; edge ports use PortFast + BPDU Guard so a rogue switch is err-disabled instead of moving the root.

rationale.subject: Link aggregation
rationale.justification: Uplinks needing > 10 Gb/s are bundled with LACP so STP sees one logical port (no blocked member) and all members carry traffic.

rationale.subject: ACL GUEST-ISOLATION
rationale.justification: Applied inbound on the VLAN 40 gateway interface, i.e. it filters traffic sourced from hosts in that VLAN. 4 entries, most specific first, ending in an explicit deny so denied flows are logged. Wildcard masks are computed bitwise from each subnet prefix (wildcard = ~mask & 0xFFFFFFFF).

rationale.subject: ACL PROTECT-MGMT
rationale.justification: Applied outbound on the VLAN 99 gateway interface, i.e. it filters traffic destined to hosts in that VLAN. 7 entries, most specific first, ending in an explicit deny so denied flows are logged. Wildcard masks are computed bitwise from each subnet prefix (wildcard = ~mask & 0xFFFFFFFF).
